title: Lawrence of Arabia (1962)
description_block: This epic British film is based on the life of T. E. Lawrence. It was directed by David Lean and produced by Sam Spiegel. The film stars Peter O'Toole in the title role, together with Alec Guinness, Anthony Quinn and Omar Sharif. It is widely considered one of the greatest and most influential films in the history of cinema. The dramatic score by Maurice Jarre and the Super Panavision 70 cinematography by Freddie Young are also highly acclaimed. It was nominated for ten Academy Awards and won seven. It won four BAFTA awards and five Golden Globes. In 1990, the year before David Lean died, Lean was awarded the American Film Institute Life Achievement Award.

title: The Hustler (1961)
description_block: When the film was first released in 1961 the US one sheet poster showed Paul Newman and Piper Laurie in an embrace, which did not have much to do with the film. However, when the film was re-released in 1966, a new more fitting poster was designed. This classic 1960s pool hustling film was directed by Robert Rosse, and stars Paul Newman as 'Fast' Eddie and Jackie Gleason as Minnesota Fats, together with Piper Laurie as Sarah.

title: The Graduate (1967)
description_block: This size poster was used for special displays and drive-ins. It was printed on heavier paper stock and far fewer were printed than the standard one sheet. It was distributed unfolded, and many got folded over time. This particular example has remained in its original unfolded state. This classic Dustin Hoffman, Anne Bancroft and Katharine Ross film, with its memorable soundtrack performed by Simon and Garfunkel was directed by Mike Nichols, who won an Academy Award for Best Director.

title: The Great Escape (1963)
description_block: This epic film, set in a prisoner of war camp during World War II, was based on Paul Brickhill's 1950 book of the same name. The film was produced and directed by John Sturges, and has an incredible cast including Steve McQueen, James Garner, Richard Attenborough, James Donald, Charles Bronson, Donald Pleasence, James Coburn, and Hannes Messemer. At the time of the film's release it was the highest grossing film of the year.

There is a perspex window on the back of the frame showing an NBC TV snipe, with information that the film was shown over two days 22nd/23rd February 1968. title: The Italian Job (1969)
description_block: This larger format poster was printed in two sheets and joined when linen backed. It features artwork unique to the film's Japanese release. This film was directed and produced by Norman Jewison, and stars Steve McQueen and Faye Dunaway. There is great on-screen chemistry between McQueen and Dunaway. McQueen plays the charming business man Thomas Crown, who thinks that he has accomplished the perfect multi-million dollar robbery, until he meets Vicki Anderson (insurance investigator), played by Dunaway, who has been employed to investigate the robbery. Here he has certainly met his match. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Song for "The Windmills of Your Mind" by Michel Legrand (music), Marilyn Bergman and Alan Bergman (lyrics).

title: Cool Hand Luke (1967)
description_block: This film was directed by Stuart Rosenberg, and stars Paul Newman and features George Kennedy, who won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actor. Newman had the leading role as Luke, who was sentenced to two years in a Florida prison, and who refused to comply with the rules. The film contains one of cinema's well known scenes, where Luke eats fifty hard boiled eggs in just one hour! It also has one of the most memorable lines said by the Captain to Luke, "what we've got here is failure to communicate."

title: Bullitt (1968)
description_block: This larger format poster was printed in two sheets and joined when linen backed. It features artwork unique to the film's Japanese release. This action thriller was directed by Peter Yates, and stars Steve McQueen, Robert Vaughn and Jacqueline Bisset. It is undoubtedly Steve McQueen's most famous role, where he plays San Francisco Police Lieutenant Frank Bullitt. Bullitt and his team are given the important task of guarding, who they think is, mobster Johnny Ross over the weekend, as Ross is due to give evidence on the Monday, in a Senate subcommittee hearing on organised crime. Things don't go quite to plan when two hitmen burst in and shoot Ross, who later dies in hospital. Bullitt is then determined to find who was behind killing the witness in his protection, and in doing so a bigger story unfolds. The other star of the film is the 1968 Ford Mustang, which Bullitt drives in the exciting, and now classic car chase scenes.

title: Bonnie and Clyde (1967)
description_block: This 1960s American crime film was directed by Arthur Penn and stars Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway as Clyde Barrow and Bonnie Parker, outlaws and lovers operating in the American South during the Great Depression. The cast also includes Michael J. Pollard, Gene Hackman and Estelle Parsons. The screenplay was written by David Newman and Robert Benton, with uncredited contributions from Beatty and Robert Towne. Beatty also produced the film.

title: Per un Pugno di Dollari / A Fistful of Dollars (1964)
description_block: This is one of the rarest posters on this classic Spaghetti Western. This film was a remake of Akira Kurosawa's 1961 film Yojimbo . When the film was initially released in Italy in 1964, Serge Leone's name wasn't used on the Italian poster, and instead the name Bob Robinson was used, to make it appear more American. The image of Clint Eastwood on the Italian poster looked nothing like him, as he was unknown in Italy. This film launched the dollar trilogy, establishing Leone and Eastwood's careers.

title: Il Buono Il Brutto Il Cattivo / The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966)
description_block: It is hard to find this poster in such good condition, owing to the fact that it is printed with a silvery background, which is difficult to keep in such pristine condition. This film was the final in the dollars trilogy, preceded by A Fistful of Dollars and For a Few Dollars More. Although at the time of release the film didn't receive great critical acclaim, it is now considered one of the greatest westerns of all time.

title: Blow-Up (1966)
description_block: This cult classic was directed by Michelangelo Antonioni, and is about a fashion photographer, played by David Hemmings, who captures a murder on film whilst taking photos in a deserted park. The film also stars Vanessa Redgrave, Sarah Miles, John Castle and Jane Birkin. Blow-Up was Michelangelo Antonioni's provocative mystery set in London's trendy swinging sixties. It became an international critical and commercial success. David Hemmings is the hot photographer, whose models include the very in demand real-life model, Veruschka. After shooting her in a sensual session, they meet at a party, where Hemmings says, "I thought you were in Paris." Veruschka, obviously high, then delivers what is arguably the most famous line in the film, "I am in Paris."

title: Une Femme est une Femme / A Woman is a Woman (1961)
description_block: This poster was signed by Anna Karina when she was a special guest at the BFI, London. This French film was written and directed by Jean-Luc Godard, and stars Anna Karina, Jean-Claude Brialy and Jean-Paul Belmondo. Anna Karina plays a striptease artist, who really wants to have a child. She tries to persuade her boyfriend to father the child, but he is not interested. Her decision is complicated as her boyfriend's best friend is in love with her.

title: La Dolce Vita (1960)
description_block: Georgio Olivetti's La Dolce Vita poster is one of the most famous images from the 60s. The poster exploits Marcello's infatuation with the starlet, conveyed quite evocatively in the dangling cigarette, its burning tip and the rising smoke. This poster was printed in two sheets and designed to be pasted onto billboards. Therefore only unused copies survived. This poster is one of the finest examples of this piece to have surfaced in recent years. It was only discovered recently in its original folded state and then linen backed. It had not been opened for over fifty years and the colours are incredibly vibrant. Perhaps no film has ever managed to capture the spirit - perhaps even the flavour - of the generation that begot it as Fellini's masterpiece La Dolce Vita . From the opening shot of Marcello Mastroianni in a helicopter flying above Rome with a massive statue of Christ hanging beneath, to Anita Ekberg's iconic early morning dip in the Fontana de Trevi.

title: Un Homme et une Femme / A Man and a Woman (1966)
description_block: This French film written and directed by Claude Lelouch and stars Anouk Aimée and Jean-Louis Trintignant. The film is highly regarded for its rich photography, which moves between black and white, colour and sepia sequences.

title: Jules et Jim (1962)
description_block: This film was directed, produced and written by François Truffaut, and is based on Henri-Pierre Roché's 1953 semi-autobiographical novel of the same name. Jules et Jim is considered one of the key films in the development of the French new wave movement.

title: La Notte / The Night (1961)
description_block: This poster was printed in two sheets and designed to be pasted onto billboards. Therefore only unused copies survived. This rare Italian poster does not surface very often. This Italian film was directed by Michelangelo Antonioni. The cast includes Marcello Mastroianni, Jeanne Moreau and Monica Vitti. The film follows an unhappy and unfaithful married couple during one entire day and night, as they confront their failing relationship and the empty world that they inhabit.

title: Belle de Jour (1967)
description_block: This is the rarer Japanese size poster, which was printed in two sheets and joined when linen backed. It features artwork unique to the film's Japanese release. This film was directed by Luis Buñuel, and stars Catherine Deneuve in one of her most famous roles. Deneuve plays a young woman who spends her midweek afternoons as a high-class prostitute while her husband is at work.

title: Les Parapluies de Cherbourg / The Umbrellas of Cherbourg (1964)
description_block: This French romantic drama was directed and written by Jacques Demy and stars Catherine Deneuve and Nino Castelnuovo. The story focuses on young lovers Geneviève Emery (Catherine Deneuve) and Guy Foucher (Nino Castelnuovo), and is presented in four parts, with the entire dialogue being sung. The music was composed by Michel Legrand.

title: Zazie Dans le Metro / Zazie W Metro (1960)
description_block: This French surrealist slapstick comedy was directed by Louis Malle, and is based on the 1959 novel of the same name by Raymond Queneau. Packed with visual and verbal humour, it follows a cast of eccentric, ever-changing characters roaming a busy Paris during a Métro strike.

title: Girl with Green Eyes / La Muchacha de los Ojos Verdes (1964)
description_block: Exceptionally rare Cuban poster. This British romantic drama was directed by Desmond Davis and stars Peter Finch, Rita Tushingham, Lynn Redgrave and Julian Glover. Adapted by Edna O’Brien from her novel The Lonely Girl , it follows a naïve young woman from the countryside who becomes involved with a sophisticated older man. Shot in black and white, her green eyes are never seen, and the film explores their developing relationship.

title: The Party (1968)
description_block: This comedy film was directed by Blake Edwards and stars Peter Sellers and Claudine Longet. This was the only film outside of the Pink Panther films that Sellers and Edwards worked together.

title: Playtime (1967)
description_block: This unique piece of artwork was used to create the Italian film poster. On the right-hand side of the artwork is a partial clear film overlay containing the title and film information. This comedy was directed by Jacques Tati, where he again plays the popular Monsieur Hulot, and is considered a masterpiece of Tati's work. It is made up of six sequences, each linked by two characters, who encounter one another over and over during the course of a day.

title: Les Vacances de Monsieur Hulot / Monsieur Hulot's Holiday (1953)
description_block: Original French release posters on this film are highly sought-after and very rarely surface. This French comedy directed and starring Jacques Tati, introduced us to Monsieur Hulot - the pipe-smoking, endearingly clumsy character. In this film Monsieur Hulot visits a seaside resort for a summer holiday. His well-meaning but bumbling behaviour unintentionally disrupts the peaceful routines of fellow guests, leading to a series of charming, whimsical mishaps. With minimal dialogue and a gentle, observational humour, the film captures the quirks of everyday life and the subtle peculiarities of social behaviour.

title: Mon Oncle (1958)
description_block: The multi-talented Pierre Etaix directed films for over forty years, and also starred in films for six decades. Etaix met Jacques Tati in 1954 and worked as a draftsman and gagman on Mon Oncle , and also designed this iconic poster, which does not surface very often. This 1958 comedy was the first of Tati's films to be released in colour, and won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

title: La Strada / Silnice (1954)
description_block: Jiri Balcar's design was unique to the film's Czech release. Only five hundred posters were originally printed. Only a small quantity are known to have survived. This film was directed by Federico Fellini from his own screenplay, which he co-wrote with Tullio Pinelli and Ennio Flaiano. The film stars Anthony Quinn and Giulietta Masina. In 1957 the Academy Awards introduced Best Foreign Language Film, which La Strada won.

title: Barbarella (1968)
description_block: This very cool artwork was only used for the Japanese release of the film. This 60s science fiction film was directed by Roger Vadim, and was based on the comic series of the same name by Jean-Claude Forest. Vadim tried to cast various actors in the title role, including Virna Lisi, Brigitte Bardot and Sophia Loren, before casting his then-wife Jane Fonda as the space-traveller Barbarella.

title: Attack of the 50 Foot Woman (1958)
description_block: This science fiction horror film was directed by Nathan Juran. The cast includes Allison Hayes, William Hudson and Yvette Vickers. Wealthy socialite Nancy Fowler Archer (Allison Hayes) is unhappily married to philandering husband Harry (William Hudson). After a close encounter with a ginormous alien, Nancy grows to a giant size and takes revenge on her cheating husband. This film has a great tagline: "A titanic beauty spreads a macabre wave of horror! A terrifying masterpiece of shock and chills!”

title: One Million Years B.C. (1966)
description_block: This is one of the most sought-after posters from the 60s, featuring striking Day-Glo lettering that was widely used throughout the 1960s and 1970s. This film is a British adventure/fantasy film set in fictional prehistoric times, and stars Raquel Welch and John Richardson. It was made by Hammer Film Productions and Seven Arts, and was a remake of the 1940 film, produced by Hal Roach Studios. The film features stop motion animation by Ray Harryhausen.

title: King Kong (1933)
description_block: Exceptionally rare. This is one of only three known surviving examples. A perfect blend of adventure, science fiction and horror, King Kong is the ultimate monster movie. Willis O'Brien's use of stop-motion effects was ground breaking for the time, and remains legendary. The film blew audiences away and broke all previous box-office records.

title: Godzilla (1954)
description_block: Original Japanese pieces on this film are highly sought-after and very rarely surface. When it comes to film, one of Japan's most famous exports is undoubtedly the sci-fi blockbuster featuring ravenous monsters. This was the very first time that audiences were introduced to Godzilla.

title: Dr. Who and the Daleks (1965)
description_block: This poster is one of the finest examples of this piece to have surfaced to date. This first Dr. Who feature film stars Peter Cushing as the Doctor, and was directed by Gordon Fleming. The daleks still remain the public's most popular enemy.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968)
description_block: Stanley Kubrick's landmark science fiction film is still considered one of the most influential sci-fi films of all time.

title: E.T. the Extra Terrestrial (1982)
description_block: Steven Spielberg's E.T. has won the hearts of so many people since its release in 1982. At the time it was the highest grossing film, surpassing Star Wars (1977).

title: Back to the Future (1985)
description_block: Back to the Future was directed by Robert Zemeckis and written by Zemeckis and Bob Gale. It stars Michael J. Fox, as teenager Marty McFly, who accidentally travels back in time from 1985 to 1955. Christopher Lloyd plays the eccentric scientist Dr. Emmett 'Doc' Brown, a friend and the inventor of the time-traveling modified DeLorean, who helps Marty reconstruct history and return to 1985. The sequel was directed by Robert Zemeckis and written by Bob Gale, and is the second film in the popular Back to the Future trilogy. Like the first film, this sequel also stars Michael J. Fox as Marty McFly and Christopher Lloyd as Dr. Emmett Brown. This film was filmed back-to-back with the final film, and was ground-breaking for its visual effects by Industrial Light & Magic (ILM).

title: Akira (1988)
description_block: This is an original Japanese theatrical premium poster produced by Tokyo Movie Shinsha / the Akira Production Committee and merchandise maker Movic, with oversight from Kodansha, for the first Japanese release of Katsuhiro Otomo’s landmark feature film Akira . Issued around the July 1988 premiere, it was printed on distinctive coarse brown 'tea paper' and offered to cinema-goers as an exclusive admission bonus only at the film's premiere. This is a very rare poster as it had a small print run as it was only offered at the film's premiere.  This Japanese animated cyberpunk film was directed by Katsuhiro Otomo, and written by Otomo and Izo Hashimoto, based on Otomo's 1982 manga of the same name. The film is set in a dystopian 2019. After the destruction of Tokyo in 1988, Neo-Tokyo is established as a futuristic metropolis. The city is cursed by corruption, anti-government protests and terrorism. A military complex is threatened by a psychic psychopath, who acquired amazing telekinetic powers after a motorbike accident, and which he uses for malicious purposes. His powers are the same as Akira, the instrument that originally destroyed Tokyo. Will history repeat itself once again?

title: Batman: The Movie (1966)
description_block: This rare Australian poster does not surface very often. This film was based on the Batman television series, and was the first full-length feature film adaptation of the DC Comics' character Batman. The film stars Adam West as Batman and Burt Ward as Robin. The film was released two months after the last episode of the first season of the television series. The film included most members of the original television cast.

title: Grand Prix (1966)
description_block: This fictional popular motor racing film is the story of the 1966 Formula One season through the eyes of four Formula One drivers The film includes real-life motor racing footage and cameos by several Formula One World Champions, including Juan Manuel Fangio, Phil and Graham Hill and Jack Brabham. The film was directed by John Frankenheimer, and stars James Garner, Eva Marie Saint and Yves Montand.

title: Le Mans (1971)
description_block: This film, directed by Lee H. Katzin, portrays the famous Le Mans 24 Hour endurance motor race, and stars Steve McQueen. It was shot on location at the Le Mans circuit between June and November 1970.

title: Enter the Dragon (1973)
description_block: This film stars the legendary martial arts actor Bruce Lee, and was his final film before his premature death the same year. The film was released in Hong Kong six days after his death.

This action adventure film was directed by Steven Spielberg. It was written by Lawrence Kasdan from a story by George Lucas and Philip Kaufman. It was the first instalment of the hugely popular Indiana Jones film franchise, which stars Harrison Ford as archaeologist Indiana Jones.

title: Jaws (1975)
description_block: Jaws invented the summer blockbuster and was a massive hit that shattered box office records. It was the film that propelled Steven Spielberg to international fame, and frightened a whole generation out of the water.

description_block: Door panels were produced in very small quantities and only used in premium cinemas. This British film was directed by Freddie Francis, and was the fourth film in the Dracula series produced by Hammer Film Productions. It was the third time that Christopher Lee played Count Dracula. The cast also includes Rupert Davies, Veronica Carlson and Barry Andrews. Count Dracula is unintentionally resurrected by a clergyman who exorcises Dracula's castle.

title: Animal House (1978)
description_block: Artwork: This is a unique piece of finished artwork for the finished British 41 x 27 in. poster. It features the artwork, without the wording or credits. It was executed in sections, with the five portraits all done individually, with the overlay artwork, including the frames, laid on the top.  This modern classic comedy was directed by John Landis, and stars John Belushi in his first film role. The film is about a misfit group of fraternity members who challenge the authority of the dean of Faber College.

title: Ferris Bueller's Day Off (1986)
description_block: This poster has become one of the most sought-after posters from the decade. This 80s film has become a true cult classic teen coming-of-age film.

title: Revenge of the Pink Panther (1978)
description_block: This was the sixth film in the popular Pink Panther comedy series, and was the last on-set performance released during the lifetime of Peter Sellers.

title: Dr. No (1962)
description_block: This was the very first James Bond film, and paved the way for a hugely successful series of films, which continues today. This film was produced by Eon Productions, directed by Terence Young and stars Sean Connery and Ursula Andress. It was based on the 1958 novel of the same name by Ian Fleming. Although made on a low budget, this film established many themes that are iconic and synonymous with Bond films.

title: Diamonds are Forever (1971)
description_block: This was the seventh in the James Bond series produced by Eon Productions, and the sixth and final Eon film to star Sean Connery. The film was directed by Guy Hamilton, in the second of four Bond films that he would direct. The film was based on Ian Fleming's novel that was published in 1956.

title: The Man with the Golden Gun (1974)
description_block: Very rare advance German poster that hardly ever surfaces. This was the ninth film in the series produced by Eon Productions. It was the second time that Roger Moore played James Bond, and the fourth and final time that Guy Hamilton would direct a Bond film. Christopher Lee plays the villain Francisco Scaramanga, whose golden gun is one of the most memorable Bond film props. The golden gun was made from Scaramanga's fountain pen, cigarette lighter, cigarette lighter and cufflinks - all made of gold. This film was loosely based on Ian Fleming's novel, published in 1965.

title: The Spy Who Loved Me (1977)
description_block: This was the tenth of the James Bond films produced by Eon Productions, and the third starring Roger Moore. It was directed by Lewis Gilbert and also stars Barbara Bach, Curt Jürgens, and Richard Kiel in the memorable role of Jaws. It captured the imagination of everyone who saw it, with Bond's famous Lotus Esprit which converts into a submarine.

title: Octopussy (1983)
description_block: This is the thirteenth film in the James Bond series produced by Eon Productions, and the sixth to star Roger Moore as James Bond. It was directed by John Glen, and also stars Maud Adams and Louis Jourdan.

title: A View to a Kill (1985)
description_block: This is the fifteenth Bond film, and the fourteenth to be produced by Eon Productions. It was the seventh and last Bond film to star Roger Moore, and last to star Lois Maxwell as Miss Moneypenny. The film was the third Bond feature to be directed by John Glen.

title: Pinocchio (1940)
description_block: This charming Danish poster is exceptionally rare, and has only surfaced a few times. Walt Disney's second animated feature film was made after the success of Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937). Pinocchio, the world’s most famous wooden puppet, is originally the creation of the Italian writer and social commentator Carlo Collodi. Entitled The Adventures of Pinocchio , the story was initially serialized in the children’s section of a Roman newspaper and, following its popularity, became a book in 1883. When Walt Disney decided to adapt the story to film, Pinocchio had already climbed to widespread fame, but it was not until he was animated that the naughty wooden boy truly became embedded in the popular imagination.

title: Bambi (1942)
description_block: Disney's fifth animated feature film Bambi was based on the book Bambi, A Life in the Woods , by Felix Salten. The film tells the story of a young deer, Bambi, growing up in the forest with his friends Thumper, Flower and Faline. Bambi's father is the Great Prince of the Forest, and protects the woodland creatures from hunters. Sweet Bambi will eventually take over this title and its responsibility. Disney changed the species of deer from a roe deer to a mule deer, as these are more common in America.

title: Springtime for Thomas
description_block: Posters from the Tom and Jerry series are highly collectable, and the ones from the 40s do not surface very often. This seven minute cartoon would have been shown before the main feature at the cinema. Tom and Jerry cartoons were extremely popular, and in the 40s nearly fifty of these shorts were produced. This animation was directed by William Hanna and Joseph Barbera.

title: Alice in Wonderland / Alice au Pays des Merveilles (1951)
description_block: Exceptionally rare French poster. This is only the second example to have surfaced to-date. It was previously in a private French collection for over twenty years. Alice in Wonderland was released in 1951 by Walt Disney, and is based on the Alice books by Lewis Carroll. It was the thirteenth animated film that Disney made. Walt Disney had attempted to make the film during the 1930s, and then revived his idea ten years later. The film was originally intended to be a mix between live-action and animation, but in 1946 Disney decided to make it completely animated. The film was not popular when released, and this led Disney to televise it on the inaugural episode of his series Disneyland . Owing to its huge popularity on television, it was re-released in cinemas around the world in the 70s, and became a colossal success.

title: Lady and the Tramp (1955)
description_block: This Disney musical animation was their fifteenth animated feature film, and was the first feature filmed in the CinemaScope widescreen film process.

title: One Hundred and One Dalmatians (1961)
description_block: This film was based on the 1956 novel The Hundred and One Dalmatians by Dodie Smith. It was Walt Disney's seventeenth animated feature film, and a much needed box-office success for the studio, after the more expensive and under performing Sleeping Beauty two years earlier.

title: Tintin et les Oranges Bleues (1964)
description_block: This French film was the second live action film based on the famous comic books The Adventures of Tintin . The film was directed by Philippe Condroyer and starred Jean-Pierre Talbot as Tintin.

title: The Jungle Book (1967)
description_block: This is a unique piece of Disney artwork used to create the US six sheet film poster. The Jungle Book , by Rudyard Kipling, was published in 1894. The first screen adaptation was by the Korda Brothers in 1942, followed by Walt Disney's classic 1967 animation musical, with its acclaimed soundtrack, featuring five songs by the Sherman Brothers and one song, 'The Bare Necessities' by Gilkyson. So popular is this storyline that Disney have to-date re-made it twice, first in 1994 and also in 2016.

title: Tonari no Totoro / My Neighbor Totoro (1988)
description_block: This artwork was only used for the double-bill showing of the film. Hayao Miyazaki, one of the founders of Studio Ghibli, wrote and directed this film. Studio Ghibli, which was founded in 1985, has been responsible for making so many magical animations. So popular and loved is Totoro that the studio uses it as their mascot/logo.

title: Mayo no Takkyubin / Kiki's Delivery Service (1989)
description_block: This Japanese animated film was written, produced, and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, and was an adaptation of the 1985 novel of the same name by Eiko Kadono. It was made by Studio Ghibli, and was the first film released under a fifteen year distribution partnership they had with The Walt Disney Company. It is a coming-of-age film, which tells the story of a young witch, Kiki, who moves to a new town during her mandatory year of independent living. She finds it difficult to fit into her new community, and supports herself by running an air courier service.

title: Who Framed Roger Rabbit (1988)
description_block: This special foil Gold Mylar poster of Jessica Rabbit with the classic tagline "I'm not bad, I'm just drawn that way," was created by Kilian Enterprises in 1988 under license from the studio. There were two different styles designed by Kilian Enterprises, and this one is the more sought-after owing to its great tagline. This live-action/animated comedy was directed by Robert Zemeckis, and stars Bob Hoskins, Christopher Lloyd, Charles Fleischer, Stubby Kaye and Joanna Cassidy. The film is set in stylish 1940s Hollywood where cartoon characters and people co-exist. Roger Rabbit has been accused of murder, and needs the help of the toon-hating detective to prove his innocence.

title: Cleopatra (1917)
description_block: This was the first adaptation of the film starring Fox Studio's biggest female star of the silent era and one of cinema's early sex symbols Theda Bara, nicknamed "The Vamp." To-date no other example of this poster is known to have surfaced.   This biographical drama has been a favourite subject of studios throughout film history, with notable leading ladies playing Cleopatra. These include Theda Bara in 1917, Claudette Colbert in 1934 and Elizabeth Taylor in 1963.

title: Blonde Venus (1932)
description_block: This rare 1930s Marlene Dietrich poster has only surfaced a few times. This American pre-Code drama stars Marlene Dietrich, Herbert Marshall and Cary Grant. It was produced, edited and directed by Josef von Sternberg from a screenplay by Jules Furthman and S. K. Lauren, adapted from a story by Furthman and von Sternberg. The original story "Mother Love" was written by Dietrich. The film follows a cabaret singer who becomes involved with a millionaire in order to fund a life-saving operation for her seriously ill husband.

title: Roman Holiday / Vacanze Romane (1953)
description_block: This poster was printed in two sheets and designed to be pasted onto billboards. Therefore only unused examples survived. Exceptionally rare Italian poster that hardly ever surfaces. This romantic comedy was directed and produced by William Wyler, and stars Audrey Hepburn and Gregory Peck. Hepburn won an Academy Award for Best Actress for her performance. The film also won two other Oscars for the screenplay and costume design.

title: Sabrina (1954)
description_block: Exceptionally rare Italian photobusta that hardly ever surfaces. This beautiful film was directed by Billy Wilder, and was an adaptation of the screenplay Sabrina Fair , written by Samuel A. Taylor. The play ran on Broadway in 1953. The film stars Audrey Hepburn, Humphrey Bogart and William Holden. The famous costume designer Edith Head won an Oscar for Best Costumes, but it was rumoured that most of Hepburn's outfits had been created by Hubert de Givenchy, who became a close friend of Hepburn.

title: Funny Face (1956)
description_block: This rare Japanese poster is one of the most beautiful pieces from any of Audrey Hepburn's films. This musical romance was directed by Stanley Donen and written by Leonard Gershe, and features numbers by George and Ira Gershwin. Audrey Hepburn stars alongside Fred Astaire, who was in the original 1927 Broadway show of the same name.

title: Breakfast at Tiffany's / Colazione da Tiffany (1961)
description_block: Ercole Brini has brilliantly captured Holly Golightly (Audrey Hepburn). This poster was printed in two sheets and designed to be pasted onto billboards. Therefore only unused examples survived. This film was directed by Blake Edwards, and stars Audrey Hepburn and George Peppard. This is undoubtedly Hepburn's most famous and iconic role.

title: Breakfast at Tiffany's (1961)
description_block: This film was directed by Blake Edwards, and stars Audrey Hepburn and George Peppard. This is undoubtedly Hepburn's most famous and iconic role.

title: Breakfast at Tiffany's (1961)
description_block: This larger format poster was used for drive-ins and special displays. Far fewer were printed than the standard one sheet posters. It was printed on heavier paper stock and distributed rolled. Over time many of these posters got folded. This particular poster has remained in its original unfolded state. This is only the fourth example of this poster to have surfaced to-date. This film was directed by Blake Edwards, and stars Audrey Hepburn and George Peppard. This is undoubtedly Hepburn's most famous and iconic role.

title: My Fair Lady (1964)
description_block: This American musical was written by Alan Jay Lerner and directed by George Cukor. It was an adaptation of the famous stage musical, which was based on the 1913 stage play Pygmalion by George Bernard Shaw. The film stars Audrey Hepburn as Eliza Doolittle, and Rex Harrison as Professor Henry Higgins, and features fantastic musical numbers. The film won eight Academy Awards.

title: Ariane (1931)
description_block: Owing to the large format of this poster it was printed in four sheets and the only way it could have been displayed would have been to paste it up to a billboard.  To-date this is the only known surviving example. This German drama was directed by Paul Czinner, and stars Elisabeth Bergner, Rudolf Forster and Annemarie Steinsieck. It is based on Claude Anet’s 1920 novel 'Ariane, jeune fille russe'. Alternative-language versions, The Loves of Ariane and Ariane, jeune fille russe , were produced at the same time. The film tells the story of a young student, Ariane, who falls for an older, charming man in Berlin and pretends to be more experienced to win him over. After he treats their affair as a mere fling and leaves her, she plans revenge, but when they meet again, they confess their true feelings and ultimately reunite. The film later inspired Billy Wilder’s Love in the Afternoon (1957). Wilder remembered the film as "touching and funny."

title: How to Marry a Millionaire / Come Sposare Un Milionario (1953)
description_block: Enzo Nistro's design for this piece is by far one of the greatest Marilyn Monroe posters from any of her films. This poster was printed in two sheets and designed to be pasted onto billboards. Therefore only unused copies survived. Exceptionally rare. This poster has only surfaced a few times. This American romantic comedy was directed by Jean Negulesco and written and produced by Nunnally Johnson. The film stars Betty Grable, Marilyn Monroe and Lauren Bacall as three New York models in search of wealthy husbands. They star alongside William Powell, David Wayne, Rory Calhoun and Cameron Mitchell. Although Betty Grable received top billing in the screen credits, Marilyn Monroe's name was listed first on all the film's advertising, including the film's trailer.

title: Marilyn Monroe at the Beverly Carlton Hotel (1952)
description_block: This photograph was taken at the Beverly Carlton Hotel Apartment for a LIFE cover story on 7th April 1952.   Exceptionally rare vintage photograph. It is understood that only a handful of these were originally printed.

title: The Seven Year Itch (1955)
description_block: Exceptionally rare US door panel that has only surfaced a few times. Very few of these were printed in comparison to the main posters. This is the best looking US poster on this film. The Seven Year Itch was co-written and directed by Billy Wilder, and stars Marilyn Monroe and Tom Ewell. Ewell had also starred in the Broadway production, before taking on the same role in the film, where he won a Golden Globe.

title: Grace Kelly
description_block: This transparency was created to promote the studio's leading actress. It was designed to be of a very high quality as it was sent to high-end magazines and newspapers that required a colour image, as opposed to the regular black and white production stills. A tiny quantity of these were produced. This transparency is conservation framed in a bespoke LED light box with UV plexiglass, with UK and US mains plug and leads. The images show the light box both on and off.

title: The Outlaw (1943)
description_block: Exceptionally rare British poster. There are fewer than ten known surviving examples. This film was produced and directed by Howard Hughes, and stars Jack Buetel, Thomas Mitchell and Jane Russell. It tells the story of Pat Garrett, Doc Holliday and Billy the Kid. This film was Russell's breakthrough role, and turned her into an instant Hollywood sex symbol.

title: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof (1958)
description_block: This film was based on Tennessee Williams' Pulitzer Prize-winning play of the same name. It was directed by Richard Brooks, and stars Elizabeth Taylor and Paul Newman, both of whom were nominated for Oscars.

title: The Sound of Music (1965)
description_block: Maria von Trapp's memoir The Story of the Trapp Family Singers , about her family during World War II, inspired the 1959 stage musical, composed by Richard Rodgers with lyrics by Oscar Hammerstein II. This film directed by Robert Wise, and starring Julie Andrews and Christopher Plummer, was an adaptation of the stage musical, and also features its well known songs. The film won a total of five Oscars, including Best Film and Best Director, and Irwin Kostal also won Best Music (Scoring of Music – Adaptation or Treatment).

title: Singin' in the Rain (1952)
description_block: This romantic comedy musical was directed and choreographed by Gene Kelly and Stanley Donen. It also stars Kelly, Donald O'Connor, and Debbie Reynolds. It shows Hollywood in the late 1920s, and the transition from the silent era to talkies, through the experiences of its three main stars.

title: Singin' in the Rain (1952)
description_block: This romantic comedy musical was directed and choreographed by Gene Kelly and Stanley Donen. It also stars Kelly, Donald O'Connor, and Debbie Reynolds. It shows Hollywood in the late 1920s, and the transition from the silent era to talkies, through the experiences of its three main stars.

title: High Society (1956)
description_block: This wonderful musical was a remake of the 1941 film The Philadelphia Story , starring Frank Sinatra, Bing Crosby, Grace Kelly and Louis Armstrong. The film has a timeless soundtrack by Cole Porter, including “High Society,” “Who Wants to be a Millionaire” and “Now You Has Jazz.”

title: Cabaret / Kabaret (1972)
description_block: This musical drama, set amongst the backdrop of 1931 Berlin and the shadow of the growing Nazi party, was directed by Bob Fosse, and stars Liza Minnelli as Sally Bowles, a flamboyant cabaret performer; Michael York, a Cambridge University student; and Joel Grey, the fantastic Master of Ceremonies at the Kit Kat Klub. “Life is a cabaret, oh chum, come join the cabaret!”

title: Love Me Tender (1956)
description_block: This was Elvis Presley's acting debut, and the only time in his acting career that he would not receive top billing. This black and white film was directed by Robert D. Webb.

title: Grease (1978)
description_block: This American musical romantic film was directed by Randal Kleiser, and stars John Travolta as Danny, Olivia Newton-John as Sandy and Stockard Channing as Betty Rizzo. It has become a summertime favourite at outdoor cinemas, with people singing along to its fantastic soundtrack.

title: A Hard Day's Night (1964)
description_block: Exceptionally rare poster designed for use only at the film's Japanese premiere. This British musical comedy, directed by Richard Lester, was released in 1964 at the peak of Beatlemania. The film stars The Beatles and comically shows two”'regular” days in their lives.

title: A Hard Day's Night (1964)
description_block: This British musical comedy, directed by Richard Lester, was released in 1964 at the peak of Beatlemania. The film stars The Beatles and comically shows two “regular” days in their lives.

title: Help! (1965)
description_block: Exceptionally rare large format premiere poster. This musical comedy was directed by Richard Lester, after his success with A Hard Day's Night the previous year. The Beatles are the main stars of the film, however it also features many other famous actors. The film premiered on the 29th July 1965 at the London Pavilion Theatre, and a week later the film's soundtrack was released as an album.

title: Yellow Submarine (1968)
description_block: This animated musical fantasy was inspired by the song “Yellow Submarine” by John Lennon and Paul McCartney. The animation features songs by The Beatles. The Beatles appear as animated characters in the film, with their voices being done by other actors, until the final scene, when their real voices are used.

title: Woodstock (1970)
description_block: This Style C poster was used for wild pasting. Wild pastings were where posters were put up in public spaces without formal permission, typically in bold and attention-grabbing places. This landmark documentary about the Woodstock Festival, which took place in August 1969 in the town of Bethel, New York, where half a million people came together for "Three Days of Peace and Music."

title: Assassin of Youth (1937)
description_block: This rare exploitation poster does not surface very often. In 1932, the Federal Bureau of Narcotics was established under the direction of Harry J. Anslinger. He proceeded to stir the public into an anti-marijuana frenzy, perpetuating the myth that users of the drug had embarked upon an irreversible descent into an underworld of crime and loose living. In the mid 1930s, the American Journal of Medicine pronounced that marijuana users “will kill or maim without reason.” The only significant challenge to such wild statements was made by the Mayor of New York, who ordered an independent and impartial investigation into the effects of the “weed with roots in hell.” When it became clear that the investigation had concluded that marijuana had none of the crime-causing effects, Anslinger quickly destroyed all the remaining copies of their report. Exploitation has always been quick to seize upon contemporary scandals and scare stories, and the 1930s saw a massive upsurge of films dealing with the tragedy of marijuana. This film poster is a perfect example of the sensationalist and absurd propaganda ostensibly intended to stop people using the drug. The film's title was cribbed from an article written by Anslinger.

title: Hallelujah (1929)
description_block: This American pre-Code musical was directed by King Vidor and stars Daniel L. Haynes and Nina Mae McKinney. It follows a sharecropper’s troubled life and his relationship with a seductive woman. Filmed in Tennessee and Arkansas, it was one of the first major studio films with an all-black cast. It was also Vidor’s first sound film and earned him an Academy Award nomination for Best Director.

title: Broadway (1929)
description_block: Eric Rohman designed this fabulous art deco poster, featuring a Broadway dancer adorned in the New York skyline. This rare poster has only surfaced a few times. This 1929 film was directed by Paul Fejos. It was Universal's first talking film with 2-strip Technicolor sequences, which appear in the finale. The cast includes Glenn Tryon, Evelyn Brent, Paul Porcasi, Robert Ellis, Merna Kennedy and Thomas E. Jackson It tells the story of an innocent young dancer in a Broadway show, who naively becomes involved in murder and illegal activities at the club where she works. Paul Fejos designed a camera crane specifically for this film, to enable him shoot every angle with fluid movement. The crane could travel at 600 feet per minute. This innovative piece of equipment was unusual for the time.

title: Flying Down to Rio (1933)
description_block: Exceptionally rare stylish Swedish poster. The legendary dancing partnership between Ginger Rogers and Fred Astaire began with 1933’s Flying Down to Rio , a straightforwardly charming screen musical about an ill-starred romance. Though they only had supporting roles, the pair stole the show with their quick-stepping, jazzy number “Carioca.”  In 1933, the United States was still in the midst of the Great Depression, and the infectious exuberance of Astaire and Rogers’s performances could not have failed to lift the audience’s spirits. Their vivacious dancing was such a delight to watch it prompted a series of nine collaborations in only six years, earning both Astaire and Rogers enduring fame and recognition. Glamorous and airy, the Dutch theatrical poster hones in on the film’s motif of flying. In the foreground a woman in a fairy-like sliver of a dress appears to be gliding through the air. One arm trailing off the page creates the illusion of a boundless night sky beyond the borders of the frame. In the background is an image of the film’s most spectacular scene, in which dancing girls put on a dazzling show while strapped to the wings of a plane.

title: A Midsummer Night's Dream / En Midsommarnatts Drom (1935)
description_block: This exceptionally rare Swedish poster has only surfaced a few times. This film was made near the end of Max Reinhardt's career, this glittering film production of Shakespeare's play is a lavish celebration of Reinhardt's visual style. Primarily a theatre director with an illustrious record in his native Europe, Reinhardt fled to the USA after the Nazis took power in Germany. Shortly after his arrival he directed his second stage production of A Midsummer Night's Dream (the first being in 1905 in Berlin), and the following year was invited to make this film version for Warner Bros.

title: Avec le Sourire / With a Smile (1936)
description_block: The caricature on this poster beautifully captures the image of Maurice Chevalier.  This film was directed by Maurice Tourneur, and tells the story of a man's need to smile in order to succeed.

title: The Red Shoes (1948)
description_block: Original British lobby cards on this title hardly ever surface. This film was directed and produced by the legendary duo Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger. The film stars Moira Shearer, Anton Walbrook and Marius Goring, together with well known dancers from the world of ballet. The film is based on the fairy tale by Hans Christian Andersen, and tells the story of a ballerina who is torn between two men: the man she has fallen in love with, and the man who can transform her career.

title: Bringing Up Baby (1938)
description_block: This is undoubtedly one of the greatest screwball comedies of the 1930s. Posters on this title are highly sought-after and very rarely surface. This American screwball comedy was directed by Howard Hawks and stars Katharine Hepburn and Cary Grant. It follows a mild-mannered palaeontologist caught up in chaotic misadventures with a scatterbrained heiress and a leopard. The script was written for Hepburn, and filming, often delayed by on-set laughter, ran over schedule and budget.

title: A Day at the Races (1937)
description_block: Exceptionally rare. This poster has only surfaced a few times. This was the seventh Marx Brothers full-length film. It is a mad-cap story about trying to keep a sanatorium open using the hopeful winnings from a horse race, with the help of a vet posing as a doctor, a race horse owner and a handful of friends.

title: The Mark of Zorro / Il Segno di Zorro (1940)
description_block: The artist Anselmo Ballester was famous for his beautiful film poster art and designed more than five hundred posters over a 45-year period. He is known for his work with the independent distribution company Minerva Films and with BCM, a company he created with Luigi Martinati and Alfredo Capitani, which specialised in film poster design. Ballester also worked extensively for Columbia Pictures. Exceptionally rare. This poster has only surfaced a few times. This American black-and-white swashbuckler was directed by Rouben Mamoulian and produced by Darryl F. Zanuck, and stars Tyrone Power, Linda Darnell and Basil Rathbone. The film is based on Johnston McCulley’s 1919 novel The Curse of Capistrano , which introduced the masked hero Zorro.

title: Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ (1925)
description_block: This silent cinema epic celebrated its 100th anniversary last year. This American silent epic adventure film was directed by Fred Niblo and was based on the novel of the same name. The film stars Ramon Novarro in the title role. The film tells the story of Judah Ben-Hur, a Jewish prince, who was wrongly imprisoned as a result of his boyhood friend Messala's corrupt ways. Judah Ben-Hur is sent off as a galley slave, and his mother and sister are imprisoned. Owing to Judah Ben-Hur's tenacity to stay alive, he returns to his homeland, and not able to find his mother and sister, who he believes are dead, he takes revenge against Messala.

title: Gone with the Wind (1939)
description_block: Owing to WWII, the film did not get released in France until 1951. It was so popular that it had a re-release only two years later. Following the publication of Margaret Mitchell's best-selling novel, the competition to obtain screen rights for its cinematic adaptation was ferocious and the creation of the screenplay a massive task undertaken by several writers including F. Scott Fitzgerald. The result was an unprecedented commercial success, a staggering representation of Hollywood glamour of the 30s which overwhelmed audiences with lavish sets and costumes.

title: Gone with the Wind (1939)
description_block: This transparency, created for the film's re-release in 1968, was designed to be of a very high quality as it was sent to high-end magazines and newspapers that required a colour image, as opposed to the regular black and white production stills. A tiny quantity of these were produced. This transparency is conservation framed in a bespoke LED light box with UV plexiglass, with UK and US mains plug and leads. The images show the light box both on and off. Following the publication of Margaret Mitchell's best-selling novel, the competition to obtain screen rights for its cinematic adaptation was ferocious and the creation of the screenplay a massive task undertaken by several writers including F. Scott Fitzgerald. The result was an unprecedented commercial success, a staggering representation of Hollywood glamour of the 30s which overwhelmed audiences with lavish sets and costumes.

title: The Wizard of Oz (1939)
description_block: Few films have enjoyed such enduring popularity as the 1939 adaptation of L. Frank Baum's children's novel The Wonderful Wizard of Oz . Judy Garland leads a delightful kooky cast of characters through a colourful fantasy landscape, occasionally waylaid by a scheming witch or a cheery musical interlude. After being largely overlooked during her first two years at MGM, Garland established herself as a talented young actress in her performance in Oz. Her childlike features, along with charm and energy that she brought to the role of Dorothy, made her an instant hit with children and adults alike. A particularly interesting feature of the film is its close attention to colour. Technicolor had recently developed the first three-colour camera, making available a full range of colours as opposed to the red-green hues of earlier techniques. Hollywood was cautious about adopting the new technology, apart from the added expense, it was necessary to film with very bright lights, which made on-set temperatures very uncomfortable, but it broadened the creative opportunities open to the directors.

title: Suspicion / Soupcons (1941)
description_block: Bernard Lancy was a prolific creator of film posters, and designed the artwork for many notable French and foreign films. He brilliantly encapsulates the crux of the drama with his close-up portrait of Cary Grant's impassive face, and Joan Fontaine's doubting and fearful eyes.  Fewer than five known surviving examples. Suspicion applies Alfred Hitchcock's characteristic motives of suspense and psychological tension to a deteriorating marriage. A series of bewildering events lead the wife, played by Joan Fontaine, to suspect that her husband, played by Cary Grant, is plotting to kill her.

title: Notorious / Les Enchaînés (1946)
description_block: This film was directed and produced by Alfred Hitchcock, and stars Cary Grant, Ingrid Bergman and Claude Rains. It was filmed during the last year of World War II, and is a complex story of espionage during that time.

title: Rear Window (1954)
description_block: Exceptionally rare signed poster. This highly acclaimed thriller was the second of three collaborations between James Stewart and Alfred Hitchcock.

title: To Catch a Thief (1955)
description_block: The artwork on this poster is unique to the film's Japanese release. This is one of Alfred Hitchcock's highly praised thrillers. This film makes spectacular use of its Riviera setting, car chases along perilous winding roads, and romantic pauses along the glittering Mediterranean coast, which creates an effect that is both glamorous and suspenseful. The film pairs two of Hitchcock's preferred actors, Grace Kelly and Cary Grant.

title: To Catch a Thief (1955)
description_block: This is the most desirable lobby card from the US set of 8. This is one of Alfred Hitchcock's highly praised thrillers. This film makes spectacular use of its Riviera setting, car chases along perilous winding roads, and romantic pauses along the glittering Mediterranean coast, which creates an effect that is both glamorous and suspenseful. The film pairs two of Hitchcock's preferred actors, Grace Kelly and Cary Grant.

title: Vertigo (1958)
description_block: There is a blank area at the top of this window card, which would have been used by the cinemas to insert screening information. This size poster was printed on heavier paper stock and distributed unfolded. However, many over time got folded. This particular piece is in its original unfolded state. This is the fourth and final time that James Stewart would work with Alfred Hitchcock, in one of his best loved thrillers. The mood of the film was greatly enhanced by the score, which was written by Bernard Herrmann.

title: North by Northwest (1959)
description_block: This wonderful thriller was directed by Alfred Hitchcock, and stars Cary Grant, Eva Marie Saint and James Mason. The score for this film was by Bernard Herrmann, who also collaborated with Hitchcock on Psycho , The Man Who Knew Too Much and Vertigo . The film's opening title sequence was created by the legendary graphic designer Saul Bass.

title: Casablanca (1942)
description_block: There is a blank area at the top of this poster, which would have been used by the cinemas to insert screening information.  Casablanca remains one of the most famous films of all time. It was directed by Michael Curtiz, and stars Humphrey Bogart, Ingrid Bergman, Paul Henreid, Claude Rains, Conrad Veidt, Sydney Greenstreet and Peter Lorre. After Bogart's success in The Maltese Falcon (1941), Casablanca was the film that truly elevated him to global stardom.

title: The African Queen (1951)
description_block: The African Queen is a British film production, and this very rare country of origin poster is credited on the bottom border as being produced by S.P. Eagle. During the McCarthy era, thousands of Americans were accused of being communists or sympathisers, and became the subject of aggressive investigations. As Sam Spiegel was on McCarthy's blacklist, he could not use his real name and therefore went by this pseudonym. Remarkably, this was the only time that Humphrey Bogart won an Oscar. Fewer than a dozen of these posters are known to have survived. This film was directed by John Huston, and stars Humphrey Bogart, Katharine Hepburn and Robert Morley. There was an amazing chemistry between Bogart and Hepburn. The film is set in Africa during World War I, and tells the story of an unlikely coupling between a missionary (Hepburn) and Bogart, the captain of the riverboat, African Queen, who join forces to attempt to sink an infamous German warship. The majority of the film was shot on location in Uganda and the Congo, and there were numerous cases of the cast and crew enduring bouts of sickness throughout filming. Huston was criticized for risking the lives of his cast when taking them on dangerous hunting expeditions.

title: The Big Sleep (1946)
description_block: Humphrey Bogart and Lauren Bacall met and fell in love on the set of To Have and Have Not two years earlier. They starred again together in this film, which was also directed by Howard Hawks. The film was an adaptation of the 1939 novel of the same name by Raymond Chandler. Bogart plays the part of private detective Philip Marlowe, who is helped with his investigations by Vivian Rutledge played by Lauren Bacall.

title: Double Indemnity (1944)
description_block: This poster was printed in two sheets and designed to be pasted onto billboards. Therefore only unused copies survived. Far few of this size poster were printed compared to the standard one sheet poster. This film noir was directed by Billy Wilder and co-written by Wilder and Raymond Chandler. The film stars Fred MacMurray as an insurance salesman, Barbara Stanwyck as a seductive wife who wishes her husband dead, and Edward G. Robinson as an insurance analyst, whose job is to investigate bogus claims. The term “double indemnity” refers to a clause in certain life insurance policies, that doubles the pay-out for certain conditions, such as when death occurs as a result of an accident. This film is the definition of film noir, and one of the finest and most influential examples of the genre.

title: Sunset Boulevard / Boulevard du Crepuscule (1950)
description_block: This American film noir was directed and co-written by Billy Wilder, and produced and co-written by Charles Brackett. The film stars William Holden, Gloria Swanson and Errich von Stroheim. The film was nominated for eleven Oscars and won three. Swanson's performance as the faded film star Norma Desmond is spellbinding. Although she was nominated for Best Actress at the Oscars, she lost out to Olivia de Havilland in The Heiress .

title: Star Wars (1977)
description_block: Owing to the huge popularity of this film it ran continuously in the US for over one year. There were four different printings of this style A US poster. This first printing has the original NSS number of 77/21-0, while the next three have different information.  This poster was distributed both unfolded and folded. This is one of the rarer unfolded examples. This was where it all began back in 1977, when George Lucas brought us the beginning of the Star Wars empire.

title: Star Wars (1977)
description_block: George Lucas commissioned Tom William Chantrell to design this British poster. Lucas liked the final result so much that he used it for the American style C poster. However, it was designed as a landscape format poster and therefore lends itself well to this British size. This was where it all began back in 1977, when George Lucas brought us the beginning of the Star Wars empire.

title: Star Wars (1977)
description_block: This poster is slightly larger than the regular US one sheet, as it has the additional colour matching strip along the left-hand side of the poster. This was where it all began back in 1977, when George Lucas brought us the beginning of the Star Wars empire.

title: The Empire Strikes Back (1980)
description_block: This larger format poster was used for drive-ins and special displays. Far fewer were printed than the standard one sheet posters. It was printed on heavier paper stock and distributed rolled. Over time many of these posters got folded. This particular poster has remained in its original unfolded state. This is the second film in the original Star Wars trilogy, which is now also known as Star Wars: Episode V – The Empire Strikes Back . Although George Lucas did not direct this film, he wrote the story and served as executive producer.

title: Return of the Jedi (1983)
description_block: This special poster was produced by Yamakatsu, and sold in Japanese cinemas only when the film was first screened in Japan. This was the final film made in the original Star Wars trilogy, which is now the sixth film, owing to the subsequent prequel trilogy.

title: The Endless Summer (1966)
description_block: This special size poster was used to advertise the film when it was showing in small venues prior to its national release. The Endless Summer is a groundbreaking surf film, made by filmmaker and narrator Bruce Brown. It follows two surfers on a surfing trip around the world. When the film was first released it inspired many surfers to go abroad, leading to the emergence of surf and travel culture.

title: Skill, Brains and Guts (1970)
description_block: This larger format poster was used for drive-ins and special displays. Far fewer were printed than the standard one sheet posters. It was printed on heavier paper stock and distributed rolled. Over time many of these posters got folded. This particular poster has remained in its original unfolded state. This boxing documentary was directed by Jimmy Jacobs, and is about the legendary former heavyweight champion Muhammad Ali. The film was made during Ali's exile from boxing for refusing to be inducted into the US Army on religious grounds. The documentary is an overview of Ali's career to that point, and features archival footage of those associated with Ali.

title: Performance (1971)
description_block: The artwork on this poster by Vic Fair was unique to the film's 1978 re-release. This film was directed by Donald Cammell and Nicolas Roeg. James Fox plays a London gangster, who goes into hiding at the home of a reclusive rock star, played by Mick Jagger.

title: Zabriskie Point (1970)
description_block: This poster, designed by the well known American graphic designer, Milton Glaser, was Glaser's only foray into designing a poster for film. The artwork was presented to the director, Michelangelo Antonioni, who unfortunately didn't like the way that it depicted his film, which wasn't how he wanted it to be marketed, and so did not use this design for the film's American release. This special poster is a complete contrast to the main studio poster, which was used, and is far superior in design. Glaser was a prolific graphic designer, who designed many fantastic advertising posters, and is best known for his “I Love New York” logo. This American drama was directed by Michelangelo Antonioni, and stars Mark Frechette, Daria Halprin and Rod Taylor. This counterculture film was partially set at Zabriskie Point, in Death Valley, California, USA—the lowest elevation in North America. At the time of release the film was an absolute failure, but over time has gained cult status, owing to its use of music by Pink Floyd, The Youngbloods, Kaleidoscope, Jerry Garcia, Patti Page, Grateful Dead, the Rolling Stones, John Fahey and Roy Orbison, as well as its cinematography and direction.
